function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
Here’s a quick overview of some key Texas traffic laws and regulations. If you need more detail on a specific topic (e.g., seat‑belt rules, DUI penalties, or commercial vehicle requirements), just let me know! | Topic | Key Points | Notes | |-------|------------|-------| | **Seat‑Belt Use** | • All drivers and front‑seat passengers must wear seat belts.
• Rear‑seat passengers under 13 must use a seat belt or approved child restraint.
• Failure to buckle up can result in a $50 fine. | Texas has a “primary” seat‑belt law, meaning police can ticket you solely for not wearing a seat belt. | | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits apply unless otherwise indicated.
• On highways, the default speed limit is 70 mph unless posted lower.
• In school zones, the speed limit is 25 mph during school hours. | Speed limits are enforced by both primary and secondary enforcement. | | **Cell Phone Use** | • Drivers may use hands‑free devices while driving.
• Texting or using a handheld device while driving is prohibited.
• Violations can lead to a $50 fine and points on your license. | Texas has a “hands‑free” law; the penalty is the same whether you’re texting or making a call. | | **DUI / Alcohol** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal for drivers over 21.
• For drivers under 21, any detectable BAC is illegal.
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas has a “zero‑tolerance” policy for under‑age drivers. | | **Driving Under the Influence of Drugs** | • The presence of any illegal drug in the driver’s system can lead to DUI charges.
• Penalties mirror those for alcohol DUI. | Drug‑related DUI laws are enforced similarly to alcohol DUI. | | **Commercial Vehicle Regulations** | • Commercial drivers must hold a valid CDL.
• Hours‑of‑Service (HOS) rules apply to limit driving time.
• Commercial vehicles must carry a valid DOT number. | Texas follows federal HOS rules but also has state‑specific regulations for certain vehicle types. | | **School Bus Rules** | • Drivers must stop at a school bus with flashing red lights and a stop sign.
• Children must remain seated until the bus stops. | Violations can result in a $200 fine and points. | | **Pedestrian Laws** | • Pedestrians have the right of way at crosswalks.
• Drivers must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and when pedestrians are crossing at intersections. | Failure to yield can lead to fines and points. | | **Traffic Signal Violations** | • Running a red light or stop sign is a primary offense.
• Penalties include a $50 fine and points. | Texas uses a “primary” enforcement system for traffic signals. | | **Parking Regulations** | • Parking in no‑stop zones, fire lanes, or handicap spaces without proper permits is prohibited.
• Violations can result in a $50 fine and towing. | Parking tickets are issued by local municipalities. | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • All vehicles must be registered with the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV).
• Vehicles must pass an annual safety inspection. | Failure to register or inspect can lead to fines and impoundment. | | **License Plate Requirements** | • Plates must be displayed on both the front and rear of the vehicle.
• Plates must be visible and not obscured. | Violations can result in a $50 fine. | | **Use of Headlights** | • Headlights must be used from sunset to sunrise and during inclement weather.
• Failure to use headlights when required can lead to a $50 fine. | Texas law requires headlights in low‑visibility conditions. | | **Seat‑Belt Law for Children** | • Children under 13 must use a seat belt or approved child restraint.
• Failure to comply can result in a $50 fine. | Texas has a “primary” enforcement seat‑belt law. | | **Traffic Ticket Points** | • Most traffic violations add points to your driving record.
• Accumulating 12 points in 36 months can lead to license suspension. | Points are tracked by the TxDMV. | | **Traffic Ticket Appeals** | • You can appeal a ticket in court.
• Appeals must be filed within 30 days of the ticket date. | Appeals can result in dismissal or a reduced penalty. | --- ### How to Find More Specific Information 1. **Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV)** – Official rules, regulations, and forms. 2. **Texas Transportation Code** – The legal text governing all traffic laws. 3. **Local County Courts** – For specific ticket appeals or local ordinances. 4. **Texas Highway Patrol** – Enforcement details and public safety resources. If you’d like a deeper dive into any of these areas—such as the exact penalties for a specific violation, how to appeal a ticket, or the latest updates to the Texas Transportation Code—just let me know!
